preamble: Monophthongization of a nasalized [ai] diphthong to the open-mid nasal vowel [ɛ̃]. In French, Latin stressed a before a nasal (when not preceded by a palatal) became Old French /ai̯/ (manum > main, pānem > pain, famem > faim). The diphthong was nasalized and then monophthongized, /ãĩ/ > /ɛ̃/, giving Modern French /ɛ̃/, realized [æ̃] in Paris and [ẽɪ̯̃] in Quebec. Before a nasal that stayed intervocalic the diphthong became oral /ɛ/ instead (saine /sɛn/, aime /ɛm/).

examples.from: Latin pānem > Old French pain, with nasal /ãĩ/
examples.note: Wikipedia gives the change as /ãĩ/ > /ɛ̃/ for pain.
Before a nasal, Latin [aː] became /ai̯/ unless a palatalized consonant preceded it (manum, amat > OF main, aime).

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
